title: Driving our transformation with the creation of the Global Data & AI function
summary: We want to create more value, grow faster, be more efficient, and offer our customers an outstanding experience.
body_text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the world and the banking sector. At Santander, while we’ve already made significant steps, we’re taking it further: we want to transform our way of working to become an organization that thinks and acts with data, with AI a key ally in every decision and customer interaction. Our aim is clear. We want to create more value, grow faster, be more efficient, and offer our customers an outstanding experience. To achieve that, we’ve created the new Global Data & AI function, which will enable us to scale our capabilities, collaborate better across the entire Group, and increase our impact quickly. At Santander, we’re not just using AI. We’re becoming an “AI-native” institution, with the trust, scale and human touch that banking requires. Ricardo Martín Manjón, Head of Data & AI at Banco Santander We base our Data & AI strategy on three key pillars: Transforming customer experience and our operations through artificial intelligence. Making smarter decisions that draw on reliable data. Accelerating impact on the business through analytical models and tangible solutions. We’re working on a global, secure and ethical ecosystem, with robust platforms and strategic partnerships with such leading enterprises as OpenAI, Microsoft, and Amazon. Moreover, we’re going to create global AI hubs, which we’re already delivering training on and organizing our people for; and we’ll continue to strengthen our ties with startups to scale up faster and better. AI with Ricardo Martín Manjón But the real transformation isn’t just in the technology: it starts with us. Because AI empowers people. It opens the doors to a new way of working, making decisions, and creating value together. And when we combine data, technology and talented people, the sky’s the limit. The future is under way. And we’re building it together. Santander’s data & AI-first strategy accelerates | Ricardo Martín Manjón

title: The AI Revolution: How Fuel Cells Are Solving the Data Center Power Challenge
summary: A recognized pioneer in fuel cells for over two decades, Bloom Energy is already supplying over 400 MW of power generation to data centers worldwide.
body_text: The US Department of Energy (DOE) predicts energy consumption could triple by 2028 , driven primarily by AI data centers and hyperscalers that need hundreds of megawatts or even gigawatts of capacity. This rapid growth is forcing a fundamental shift in how we think about power infrastructure. And for data centers, power availability has become the primary site selection factor , leapfrogging traditional priorities like low latency and fiber connectivity. “The rapid growth of AI is driving massive demand for data center capacity,” said Camilla Rizzi of Plug and Play Tech Centers, in a recent webinar presented by the DOE’s Western Region Technical Assistance Partnership (TAP) . The webinar also included representatives from Oilon US, Bloom Energy and the DOE’s Western Region TAP. For example, Amazon alone is spending $10 billion to build just two data centers in Mississippi, Rizzi noted. Meanwhile, Meta is planning a 5-gigawatt data center the size of Manhattan in Louisiana. Spiky Loads Demand Instantaneous Response One of the biggest challenges for data center power is that AI workloads have extreme variability in their power demands. A single server’s power load might fluctuate from 15kW to 30kW within seconds, scaling up to 50-100MW swings at the data center level, according to Bloom Energy tests. In terms of capacity, that could mean going from 20% of provisioned power to 150% — and the traditional grid infrastructure can’t handle that kind of swing. Data centers need power solutions that can match the “spikiness” of those loads. Many have been addressing this by adding batteries, but batteries have a limited number of charge-discharge cycles. “Fuel cells and supercapacitors can easily handle this kind of load profile,” Bloom Energy’s Kaushal Biligiri said, noting that this combination can provide instantaneous responses to load changes, achieving 200,000+ charge cycles while maintaining 99.9% availability. Capturing Heat Drives Remarkable Efficiency Efficiency becomes a pressing concern when power is costly and time-consuming to obtain. Here, too, fuel cells have an advantage. Because solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) generate heat, it’s possible to capture that heat and use it. By combining heat and power applications, fuel cell efficiency rises from 54% to over 90% . For example, Biligiri said, “We can use fuel cells integrated with absorption chillers, generate chilled water and run it through the liquid cooling loop. That can drive a 10 to 15% improvement in the power usage effectiveness (PUE) value , which is an important sustainability metric for any data center.” In other parts of the world, industrial heat pumps are recovering massive amounts of waste heat from data centers and using it for local home and office heating. Oilon US’s Morgan Copeland noted that a Microsoft project in Helsinki uses 32 heat pumps across two data centers to supply district heating for 100,000 people. “That equates to roughly a 1% to 3% greenhouse gas emission reduction for the entire country of Finland from just two data centers,” Copeland said. Get Modular and Get Going As data centers follow utility pricing around the country (or around the globe), there’s an increasing demand for containerized, turnkey solutions to help those data centers get up and running quickly. Copeland noted that heat pumps delivered on skids are in demand because they can be delivered, installed, and brought online rapidly anywhere. Biligiri added that the same is true of modular fuel cell units: They enable rapid installation of power generation capacity. “Fuel cells arrive on site on a skid, and we just stack them on steel structures,” Biligiri said. Islands on the Rise Grid interconnection delays are pushing data centers toward island microgrids. In these cases, fuel cells run completely off-grid in load-following mode. “Every utility requires an interconnection agreement before it can accept a distributed energy resource onto its network. And that takes time,” said Biligiri. In the meantime, onsite fuel cells from Bloom Energy can operate as islanded microgrids. This means power generation is completely off-grid, with fuel cells sitting next to the data center generating power 24/7, load-following the data center’s needs. After the data center operator reaches an interconnection agreement with the utility, this microgrid can be connected to the utility’s grid. Then the fuel cells can provide supplemental power to the grid, increasing reliability and capacity for the entire region. Urban-Friendly Solutions As data centers grow, land use becomes a significant factor. This is especially important in urban or suburban locations, where real estate is at a premium. Fuel cells offer high power density, can be stacked in layers and are extremely quiet, operating at 65 decibels from 10 feet away . “You can stand next to a fuel cell while it’s generating power and have a conversation without any noise issues,” said Biligiri. There is almost no nitrogen oxide (NOX) pollution because the operating temperature of an SOFC is too low for the NOX reaction. There’s also no sulfur oxide pollution (SOX) because the sulfur-containing odorants have been filtered out before the natural gas reaches the fuel cell. And, with an enclosed system that has few moving parts, there are no volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted due to methane leaks. Efficient, Reliable Onsite Energy — Today A recognized pioneer in fuel cells for over two decades, Bloom Energy is already supplying over 400 MW of power generation to data centers worldwide . With rapidly deployable, efficient, and reliable fuel cells from Bloom, data center builders remove a major obstacle to rapid, competitive growth.

title: eHealth, Inc. Announces Inducement Grant Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
summary: AUSTIN, Texas, Oct. 3, 2025 -- eHealth, Inc. (Nasdaq: EHTH) (ehealth.com), a leading private online health insurance marketplace (the "Company"), today announced that on October 1, 2025, the Compensation Committee of its Board of Directors granted...
body_text: eHealth, Inc. Announces Inducement Grant Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) October 03, 2025 AUSTIN, Texas , Oct. 3, 2025 -- eHealth, Inc. (Nasdaq: EHTH) ( ehealth.com ), a leading private online health insurance marketplace (the "Company"), today announced that on October 1, 2025, the Compensation Committee of its Board of Directors granted an inducement restricted stock unit award to a new non-executive level employee covering an aggregate of 5,000 shares of the Company's common stock. The award was granted under the Company's Amended and Restated 2021 Inducement Plan (the "Inducement Plan") and otherwise will be subject to the terms and conditions of a restricted stock unit agreement under the Inducement Plan. The award will be subject to vesting over three years, with one-third of the shares vesting on each of the first, second and third anniversary of the award's vesting commencement date, October 1, 2025, subject to the employee's continued service with the Company through each vesting date. The restricted stock unit award was granted as an inducement material to the new employee's entering into employment with the Company in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). title: Comparing Gaming Keyboard Materials: Why Aluminum Tops Outlast Plastic
summary: Explore why Turtle Beach aluminum gaming keyboards outlast plastic ones. Learn how material choice impacts performance, feel, and the durability of your...
body_text: Your fastest combo just failed because your keyboard flexed under pressure. Your keycaps have worn smooth from months of grinding. The plastic case cracked after one too many intense gaming sessions. Sound familiar? Gaming keyboard materials directly impact performance , and choosing between aluminum vs plastic keyboard options can determine whether your setup becomes a liability or lasts for years. Whether you're building a complete gaming battlestation with precision peripherals like Turtle Beach's keyboards or upgrading from a budget membrane board, understanding mechanical keyboard materials helps you invest wisely. From durability advantages to typing feel differences, we'll explore why aluminum keyboards consistently outperform plastic alternatives in gaming environments. Introduction: Importance of Keyboard Material in Gaming Performance and Durability The foundation of your gaming setup isn't just your GPU or CPU; it's the interface between you and victory. Keyboard case materials comparison reveals significant performance differences that directly affect your competitive edge. Material choice influences everything from key stability during rapid inputs to long-term reliability under gaming stress. Gaming demands exceed typical office use. Rapid-fire inputs, extended sessions, and higher force application all accelerate wear on inferior materials. Understanding these demands helps explain why material choice significantly impacts both immediate performance and long-term value. Overview of Common Keyboard Materials: Plastic and Aluminum Modern gaming keyboard build quality centers around two primary construction materials, each with distinct characteristics that affect performance, durability, and user experience. Plastic Construction Most entry-level gaming keyboards utilize high-density plastic cases, typically ABS (Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene) or specialized polymers. Plastic keyboards are lightweight, cost-effective, and easier to manufacture in various colors and designs. They typically weigh around 1kg compared to aluminum alternatives. The material's flexibility can provide some shock absorption, though this same flexibility becomes problematic under gaming stress. Plastic cases offer significant manufacturing advantages. They can be injection-molded into complex shapes, incorporate RGB lighting diffusion, and achieve aggressive gaming aesthetics at lower production costs. However, these benefits come with performance trade-offs that become apparent during intensive gaming use. Aluminum Construction Premium aluminum keyboard case benefits stem from the material's fundamental properties. Aluminum keyboards typically weigh 1.5-2.5kg due to the material's density, providing superior stability and a premium feel that keyboard enthusiasts highly value. The material undergoes surface treatments like anodization to achieve various colors while maintaining metallic luster. Aluminum's inherent strength ensures keyboards can withstand extensive use without cracking or warping, making them reliable for both intense gaming and professional typing applications. This material choice represents a long-term investment in consistent performance. Durability Comparison: Why Aluminum Lasts Longer than Plastic Keyboard material longevity differences become stark when examining real-world gaming scenarios. Competitive gaming involves thousands of keystrokes per hour, often with above-average force application during intense moments. Structural Integrity Under Gaming Stress Plastic keyboards are more prone to wear and tear with frequent use, including a higher risk of flexing, which affects longevity . Heavy typists and gamers often find that plastic keyboards feel less stable during intense use. This instability can cause key wobble, inconsistent actuation, and eventual case failure around high-stress points. Aluminum construction eliminates these concerns. The material's rigidity prevents the flex-related issues that plague plastic keyboards during competitive gaming, while offering excellent heat dissipation and a comfortable typing experience during extended use. Long-Term Performance Retention Mechanical keyboards can last 10-15 years with proper maintenance , with aluminum cases offering protection and durability that increases overall lifespan by protecting against physical damage. This extended lifespan makes aluminum keyboards particularly valuable for serious gamers who demand consistent performance over years of use. Plastic keyboard durability limitations become apparent after 1-3 years of intensive use. Even high-quality plastic mechanical keyboards show wear patterns and flexibility increases that affect gaming performance over time, while aluminum keyboards maintain their structural integrity throughout their operational lifetime. Typing Experience: Stiffness, Weight, and Feel Differences The material foundation of your keyboard directly influences every keystroke, affecting both competitive performance and long-term comfort during extended gaming sessions. Weight and Stability Benefits Metal keyboards weigh approximately 50% more than plastic models, helping them stay in place during intense typing or gaming sessions. This added weight provides more stability during use. For competitive gamers, this stability translates to more consistent key actuation and reduced keyboard movement during rapid input sequences. The substantial weight of aluminum keyboards eliminates the sliding and shifting that commonly affects lighter plastic models. During intense gaming moments, when milliseconds matter, having a keyboard that stays exactly where you place it provides a crucial competitive advantage. Rigidity and Key Feel Aluminum cases provide rock-solid stability, critical for gamers who need precise, wobble-free keystrokes during intense gameplay. This rigidity ensures that the force applied to each key translates directly to switch actuation without energy loss through case flex. Plastic keyboards' inherent flexibility can create an inconsistent feel that affects precision. When the entire keyboard flexes under pressure, key actuation becomes less predictable, potentially causing missed inputs during critical gaming moments. Aluminum's rigidity eliminates this variability, providing consistent tactile feedback that serious gamers require. Sound Profile Differences between Aluminum and Plastic Keyboards Audio feedback plays a crucial role in gaming performance, helping players confirm successful key presses and maintain rhythm during complex input sequences. Acoustic Characteristics Plastic keyboards tend to provide a deeper sound signature, while aluminum keyboards have a mid-tone or higher-pitched sound profile. The sound varies significantly depending on the specific board design. These acoustic differences affect both user experience and environmental considerations. Rigid materials like aluminum amplify sharp, high-frequency tones, creating crisp sounds that enthusiasts associate with mechanical keyboards. Softer materials like plastic absorb vibrations, producing muted, bass-heavy sounds. The choice between these sound profiles often depends on the gaming environment and personal preference. Impact on Gaming Performance The crisp, immediate audio feedback from aluminum keyboards helps gamers confirm successful key presses during rapid input sequences. This auditory confirmation becomes particularly valuable during complex combo inputs in fighting games or rapid-fire commands in strategy games, where visual confirmation may be delayed. The definitive sound helps maintain input rhythm and confirms successful actuation even when visual attention focuses entirely on gameplay. Heat Dissipation and Performance Impact Extended gaming sessions generate heat from both internal components and friction from intensive keyboard use. Material choice significantly affects thermal management and sustained performance. Thermal Conductivity Advantages Aluminum has high thermal conductivity at 237 W/m·K compared to plastic materials, which typically range between 0.1-0.5 W/m·K . This excellent heat dissipation is particularly beneficial in gaming environments where prolonged use can generate heat buildup. For serious gamers who engage in marathon sessions, thermal management becomes a performance factor. Aluminum's superior thermal properties help prevent the temperature buildup that can affect switch performance and user comfort. Performance Sustainability Heat buildup in plastic keyboards can cause switches to feel different as temperatures rise, potentially affecting actuation force and tactile feedback. Aluminum keyboards maintain consistent performance characteristics regardless of ambient temperature or session duration, providing the reliability that competitive gaming demands. Aesthetic and Customization Options Visual appeal and personalization options significantly influence gaming setup satisfaction and long-term enjoyment. Modern gaming emphasizes both performance and style, making aesthetic considerations increasingly important. Premium Visual Appeal Aluminum keyboards offer superior tactile and visual texture through surface treatments like anodizing , which retains the metal's original luster while allowing for coloring and a premium feel. These surface treatments create distinctive appearances that plastic keyboards cannot replicate. The industrial aesthetic of aluminum keyboards complements modern gaming setups, particularly those emphasizing clean lines and premium components. When paired with quality peripherals like Turtle Beach's Vulcan II keyboards , the aluminum construction creates a cohesive high-performance gaming environment. Customization Potential CNC integrated carving technology and multiple polishing stages highlight the aluminum material feel, with anodization and sandblasting processes creating delicate matte textures. These manufacturing capabilities enable unique finishes and custom designs that differentiate premium gaming setups. Modern gaming emphasizes personalization and individual expression. Aluminum keyboards support advanced customization options through precision machining, custom engravings, and specialized finishes that help create distinctive gaming environments. Price vs Longevity: Is Aluminum Worth the Investment? Understanding the total cost of ownership helps evaluate whether aluminum keyboards provide sufficient value over their operational lifetime compared to plastic alternatives. Initial Investment Analysis Metal keyboards are expensive, with entry-level aluminum boards starting around $100 without keycaps or switches. Premium metal keyboards can cost significantly more. This upfront cost often deters budget-conscious gamers from considering aluminum options. However, focusing solely on initial price ignores long-term value considerations. When building a complete gaming setup with components like Turtle Beach's precision peripherals, considering the total ownership cost over several years provides a more accurate value assessment. Long-Term Value Proposition Mechanical keyboards with quality construction last 10-20 years with proper care , while typical keyboards need replacing after 1-3 years. A single mechanical keyboard can provide long-term reliability far exceeding multiple cheaper replacements. Investing in aluminum mechanical keyboards results in a longer product lifespan compared to plastic alternatives, with aluminum keyboards retaining higher resale value when upgrade time arrives. This retained value partially offsets the higher initial investment. Gaming-Specific Value Factors Competitive gamers face additional value considerations beyond typical office use. Tournament travel, intensive practice sessions, and streaming requirements all favor durable, reliable equipment. The cost of missed opportunities due to equipment failure often exceeds the price difference between aluminum and plastic keyboards. The best material for a gaming keyboard depends on individual priorities and gaming intensity. Casual gamers may find quality plastic keyboards sufficient, while serious competitors benefit from aluminum's performance advantages and longevity. Choosing the Right Material for Your Gaming Needs The selection of gaming keyboard materials significantly impacts both immediate performance and long-term satisfaction. Aluminum keyboards provide superior durability, thermal management, stability, and aesthetic appeal, making them ideal for serious gamers, professionals, and enthusiasts who demand consistent performance over years of use. For competitive players building comprehensive gaming setups with precision peripherals, aluminum keyboards provide the foundation stability and reliability that complement professional-grade gaming equipment. When paired with Turtle Beach's headsets and controllers , quality aluminum keyboards complete a cohesive high-performance environment. Plastic keyboard durability limitations become apparent during intensive gaming use, though budget-conscious gamers may find them adequate for casual play. The choice ultimately depends on gaming intensity, budget considerations, and long-term value priorities. When building a gaming setup designed to last, choosing quality components across all peripherals creates a cohesive environment that supports peak performance for years. Aluminum keyboards represent an investment in consistency, durability, and professional gaming excellence that serious players will appreciate throughout their gaming journey. FAQ What are the advantages of aluminum keyboards over plastic? Aluminum keyboards offer superior durability, better heat dissipation, enhanced stability during intense gaming, reduced flex for consistent key feel, premium aesthetics, and longer lifespan. They typically last 10-15 years compared to plastic keyboards' 1-3 year replacement cycle. Pair them with quality peripherals like Turtle Beach's Vulcan II keyboards for optimal performance. How long do aluminum gaming keyboards last? With proper maintenance, aluminum mechanical keyboards can last 10-20 years. The aluminum case protects internal components from physical damage, while the material's durability prevents cracking, warping, or degradation that affects plastic keyboards over time. Are plastic gaming keyboards less durable than aluminum ones? Yes, plastic keyboards are significantly less durable. They're more prone to flexing, cracking, and wear under intensive gaming use. Plastic keyboards typically need replacement after 1-3 years, while aluminum keyboards can function reliably for decades with proper care. Does keyboard material affect typing sound and feel? Absolutely. Aluminum keyboards produce crisp, mid to higher-pitched sounds with solid tactile feedback, while plastic keyboards generate deeper, more muted tones. Aluminum's rigidity eliminates flex that can make key presses feel inconsistent during rapid gaming inputs. Which keyboard material is better for gaming? Aluminum is superior for serious gaming due to enhanced stability, consistent key feel, better heat dissipation, and long-term reliability. While plastic keyboards are suitable for casual gaming, aluminum offers the performance consistency and durability that competitive gaming requires. Consider pairing with Turtle Beach's gaming peripherals for a complete setup.

title: TAL Education Group Announces Unaudited Financial Results for the Second Fiscal Quarter Ended August 31, 2025 and Issues Notice of Annual General Meeting

Non-GAAP cost of revenues, which excluded share-based compensation expenses, increased by 34.8% to US$628.8 million from US$466.5 million in the first six months of fiscal year 2025 . Selling and marketing expenses increased by 47.2% to US$448.1 million from US$304.3 million in the first six months of fiscal year 2025. Non-GAAP selling and marketing expenses, which excluded share-based compensation expenses, increased by 49.4% to US$442.1 million from US$296.0 million in the first six months of fiscal year 2025. General and administrative expenses increased by 9.2% to US$250.2 million from US$229.2 million in the first six months of fiscal year 2025. Non-GAAP general and administrative expenses, which excluded share-based compensation expenses, increased by 13.7% to US$234.8 million from US$206.6 million in the first six months of fiscal year 2025. Total share-based compensation expenses allocated to the related operating costs and expenses decreased by 35.9% to US$22.5 million in the first six months of fiscal year 2026 from US$35.1 million in the same period of fiscal year 2025. Gross Profit Gross profit increased by 43.3% to US$806.4 million from US$562.9 million in the first six months of fiscal year 2025. The gross margin for the first six months of fiscal year 2026 was 56.1%, compared to 54.5% in the same period of the prior year. Income from Operations Income from operations was US$110.4 million in the first six months of fiscal year 2026, compared to income from operations of US$30.3 million in the same period of the prior year. Non-GAAP income from operations, which excluded share-based compensation expenses, was US$133.0 million, compared to US$65.4 million Non-GAAP income from operations in the same period of the prior year. Other Income Other income was US$76.5 million for the first six months of fiscal year 2026, compared to other income of US$33.6 million in the same period of the prior year. Impairment Loss on Long-term Investments Impairment loss on long-term investments was US$1.4 million for the first six months of fiscal year 2026, compared to US$8.7 million for the first six months of fiscal year 2025. Income Tax Expense Income tax expense was US$62.2 million in the first six months of fiscal year 2026, compared to US$27.9 million for the first six months of fiscal year 2025. Net Income Attributable to TAL Education Group Net income attributable to TAL was US$155.4 million in the first six months of fiscal year 2026, compared to net income attributable to TAL of US$68.8 million in the first six months of fiscal year 2025. Non-GAAP net income attributable to TAL, which excluded share-based compensation expenses, was US$177.9 million, compared to US$103.9 million Non-GAAP income attributable to TAL in the same period of the prior year. Basic and Diluted Net Income per ADS Basic and diluted net income per ADS were both US$0.26 in the first six months of fiscal year 2026. Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS, which excluded share-based compensation expenses, were both US$0.30 in the first six months of fiscal year 2026. Cash Flow Net cash provided by operating activities for the first six months of fiscal year 2026 was US$289.7 million. title: Watch: Currents of Pan-Cancer - Insights from 1,000 Circulating Proteins
body_text: Comprehensive proteomic analysis offers a powerful means of understanding cancer biology and treatment outcomes. However, conventional approaches often lack the throughput, scalability, coverage, and data interoperability required for large-scale or comparative studies. Advances in high-throughput quantitative proteomics now allow scientists to precisely, rapidly, and economically analyze thousands of samples. In this webinar Lloyd Bod, PhD ( Harvard Medical School, Massachusetts General Hospital, Broad Institute) and Nathaniel Robichaud, PhD, (Nomic Bio) will discuss how large-scale profiling of the circulating proteome across multiple cancer types reveals unique tumor-specific protein signatures and provides new insights into treatment response. Topics to be covered: Exploring biomarker discovery opportunities enabled by new proteomics tools Highlighting the unique proteomic features of multiple tumor types, including pancreatic, colorectal, melanoma, and Merkel cell carcinoma Characterizing immunotherapy-specific changes in the circulating proteome Identifying proteomic markers associated with therapeutic response ‍
